Hi Vivek / Ben,

Quick note from our side — we pulled the Q3 usage numbers and there’s been a ~3.2x uplift in inference calls starting mid-July after we rolled a new feature. That puts us well above the current committed tier. Our renewal is due end of January 2028, but given this run rate we need to discuss mid-contract options so we don’t hit runaway overages.

Three asks:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary uplift path (top-up or short-term bucket) with a predictable blended price?
- Are there co-terming options to align the extra capacity to our Jan 31 renewal?
- What procurement timeline do you need to approve an amendment so we can loop in our finance/procurement?

I attached the usage export for your review (usage_report_q3.csv). Happy to hop on a short call next week — I’m available Tue/Thu mornings PT.

Thanks,
Lina
Director, AI Products
Storaly

Hi Lina — really helpful data, thanks for sending. Congrats on the product release — growth looks healthy.

High-level proposals to keep things predictable and low friction:
1) Short-term top-up (preferred for speed): add a temporary committed bucket for 3 months sized to the observed spike (we can size ~+250% over current commit). Offer an introductory 20% blended discount on tokens for the first 90 days to soften the lift, then revert to standard committed pricing.

2) Surge-credit pool (more conservative): create a rolling credit pool you draw from for surges; pricing slightly higher than committed but capped to avoid runaway overages. Quarterly true-up to align spend to commitment.

3) Co-terming: we can fold the temporary uplift into an amendment that co-terms to Jan 31, 2028. That would let you annualize the increased capacity on your next renewal and avoid duplicate contract pieces.

Operational asks from our side:
- We need an estimated baseline for the next 12 months (even a range is fine).
- Confirmation of your procurement lead and expected PO timing (so we can schedule the amendment and invoice flows).

I attached a preliminary options sheet with rough $/token math and invoice timing examples. If you’re available Tue 25 or Thu 27 morning PT I can jump on a quick 30-min call with Ben and Kimberly to walk through.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Team — recapping and recommending our approach for Storaly (this will be the doc we share as the internal ask before legal/finance drafts):

Recommended commercial path (concise):
1) Temporary uplift amendment (AMND-4527): +250% bucket for 6 months, co-term to 2028-01-31.
2) Pricing cadence: 20% blended discount for months 0–3, step-down to 10% months 4–6, then annualized committed rate after co-term. Enables Storaly to ramp while controlling unit economics.
3) Quarterly true-up and one operational true-up invoice at the end of each quarter.
4) Early-signing incentive: one-time credit equal to 5% of the first invoice if signed within Procurement’s 30-day window.

Risks / notes:
- We need legal to approve amendment language around service levels for the enlarged bucket (SLA exposure increases with higher committed capacity).
- Finance needs the first-invoice estimate to confirm PO acceptance (Lina provided expected run-rate range; use midpoint for initial invoice).
- Suggest we include a short audit clause that allows us to surface abnormal burst behavior for product teams.

Next steps: I’ll create a draft amendment (AMND-4527) with Kimberly’s pricing ops inputs and send to Legal + Lina. If we want to be aggressive, add the early-signing credit to close quickly.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
